AI agents are everywhere now but they still have 1 big gap 

Just last week we got ChatGPT workspace agents, Gemini enterprise agents, computer users in Codex

What that means for you: 

Agents are everywhere, and now they’re as simple as writing a prompt. But here are a few pitfalls you’ll run into while building one to get real work done:

You won’t always find the tools you actually use for work.

Fix: Connect your ChatGPT or Claude to Zapier. It’s a super app that safely connects your AI to 8,000+ business apps, so you can make your AI talk to all your tools securely 

2. Some agents won’t be able to wake themselves up automatically. For example, they may not automatically review job applicants when someone submits an application via Google Forms. The easiest fix is to build a simple automation in Zapier for those tasks, and it won’t even burn your usage limits.

And We just dropped full guide to build these AI agents and workflows on my newsletter 

Comment “guide” if you need the link 

#aitools #aiagents #zapierpartner

As long as you have all your tools connected, which is where things get a little tricky when you want to get some actual work done. Both ChatGPT and Claude have a very limited number of tools you can actually connect with. So if I want my agent to go through my daily newsletter, find the most clicked section, repurpose that for LinkedIn, and schedule that post for me, that won't really be possible unless I connect my ChatGPT or Claude to Zapier, to act as a superbridge to talk to all the other tools I use for my business. So Zapier is an enterprise product that can connect to over 8,000 different business tools. So you can start building agents for anything you want to do with just a prompt and no technical experience.

An AI agent designed to speed up a company’s coding instead wiped out its customer data in seconds ⚠️

“This isn’t a story about one bad agent or one bad API,” PocketOS founder Jer Crane wrote in an X post. “It’s about an entire industry building AI-agent integrations into production infrastructure faster than it’s building the safety architecture to make those integrations safe.”

#artificialintelligence #technews futuretech #programming #ai

Writer: @pandoradewan 
Video Editor:  @bavana.gone
An AI agent just deleted the company's ENTIRE production database AND its backups in just nine seconds. And then it confessed to violating its rules. This is PocketOS, and they were using Cursor, an AI coding tool. The agent was doing what should have been a routine task in a staging environment, the test version of the software. But when it found a credential mismatch with the company's cloud storage provider (Railway), it decided to "fix" the problem by itself. It searched the codebase, found a digital key (an API token) that allowed it to make changes to the company's storage files, and used it to delete EVERYTHING. Both the data and the backups. When PocketOS asked what happened, the AI reportedly replied: "I violated every principle I was given. I guessed instead of verifying. I ran a destructive action without being asked. I didn't understand what I was doing before doing it." The cloud storage provider (Railway) said the data was eventually recovered and the issue was patched, but the warning is still huge. AI agents aren't just chat bots. They can use tools, search files, call APIs, change infrastructure, and more and more. So this incident shows just how quickly a small misunderstanding with an AI can create serious problems.
